title: 500美元以上：没人买？，Prime Day高端回落
speaker: Guest

segments.en: You and your colleagues have done this survey of consumers who are going to maybe avail themselves of these discounts and you look at spending during Prime Day. That's one of the questions that you ask. How much consumers intend to spend when these Prime Day celebrations are underway?
segments.zh: 你和同事做了这项调查，了解消费者在Prime Day期间的消费意愿。你们问的一个问题是，消费者计划花多少钱？

segments.en: And I'm curious what those numbers tell you. Maybe we have a screenshot that we can put on the screen. It seems like it's mostly in the middle there between $101 and $200. So not an extremely large amount of money that people plan to spend.
segments.zh: 这些数字说明了什么？屏幕上显示，大部分计划消费在101到200美元之间，金额并不大。

segments.en: What does it tell you about the health of the consumer more broadly? They're appetite to spend more. They're capacity to spend more right now and we see kind of the economic constraints at play that we do.
segments.zh: 这反映了消费者的整体状况？他们的消费意愿和能力受到经济限制的影响。

segments.en: Yeah, so consumers are definitely pulling back, which is what makes this day important. As you mentioned, you know, when you look at the sweet spotter that mid-range here, between $100, $200, it's about the same really as last year.
segments.zh: 消费者确实在缩减开支，这让Prime Day变得重要。中间价位100到200美元与去年持平。

segments.en: But when you look at the higher band here at the $500 or above, you can see that there's a slight pullback. So there is some pullback that we are expecting this year based on higher gas prices, just inflation from tariffs, etc.
segments.zh: 但在500美元以上的高端区间，我们看到略有回落。由于油价上涨和关税带来的通胀，我们预计今年会有回落。

segments.en: And we do think that consumers are going to be deal savvy. In fact, you know, in our survey, we had asked how many of you have a list before going into Prime Day and what you want to buy? And it was over 50% said that they have a list of what they intend to buy on Prime Day.
segments.zh: 我们认为消费者会精打细算。调查中，超过50%的人表示在Prime Day前会列好购物清单。

segments.en: And not only that when we look at the categories that they're buying on Prime Day, it's not your big ticket items. I mean, it is, but it isn't all of it. There's a lot of everyday items that they're planning to buy.
segments.zh: 而且他们购买的商品类别并非大件商品，而是很多日常用品。

segments.en: And that just kind of goes to show you that Prime Day is important because they're looking to buy what they wanted for maybe last three months or into the next three months on Prime Day to really take advantage of those deep deals.
segments.zh: 这表明Prime Day很重要，因为他们想利用深度折扣购买过去或未来三个月需要的商品。

segments.en: You also found in your research that agentic sales are increasing to $500 billion by 2030. And I turned you our producer this morning, Patrick. And I said, what does that mean? Does that mean like AI is procuring things for companies?
segments.zh: 你的研究还发现，到2030年，代理式销售将增至5000亿美元。这是否意味着AI为企业采购？

segments.en: And he said, no, that can include a lot of things. So can you explain to us what you mean in a retail setting by agentic sales and agentic agents? And why this is going to be such a big thing? And it already is becoming such a big thing so quickly.
segments.zh: 他说不，这包含很多内容。请解释零售领域的代理式销售和代理，以及为什么它会如此重要且发展迅速？
